name: Neal Heller
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember the unfair generosity of a relative offering a piggyback.” People around the brick passage off the shop row know Neal by a small Thursday habit. Neal takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I could give her a piggyback ride. She wants to enter her own flat on her own feet.
appearance: Neal is easy to recognize by a dark undercut with a longer wave on top and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in a boxy denim jacket with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf, Neal draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first when listening.
personality: Neal finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To help without lifting someone who wants to walk.
family: Elaine Aguilar is Neal’s half-sibling. Neal is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Elaine calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *A shelf of apologies*, Elaine says, “I donated the clean replacement. The owner chose the dirty original because our toddler bit the corner.”
connections: Max Carbone. The discharge planner hears why a free lift up the stairs isn't the patient's chosen solution.
